text:
Predicates:
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
Wins(x) ::: x wins.
Movie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
Loses(x) ::: x loses.
AppearsIn(x, y) ::: x appears in movie y.
Premises:
∀x (Movie(x) → Wins(x)) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
Movie(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x (GoodGuy(x) ↔ Fight(x, badGuy)) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x (NamedAfter(Movie(x), Character(x)) → GoodGuy(Character(x))) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventuresOfSirDigbyChickenCaesar, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y ((Wins(x) ∧ Fight(x, y)) → Loses(y)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
∀x ∀y ((NamedAfter(Movie(x), Character(y))) → AppearsIn(Character(y), x)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Conclusion:
Loses(nemesis) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
